ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The family pedigree chart below shows a family with two monogenic genetic diseases, disease A and disease B. Disease A is a certain familial hereditary tumor, controlled by alleles A/a; disease B is phenylketonuria, caused by a lack of phenylalanine hydroxylase, controlled by alleles B/b, and the two pairs of genes are inherited independently. According to the figure, what is the mode of inheritance of disease B?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The legend shows that blank squares/circles indicate normal males/females, diagonally striped squares/circles indicate males/females with disease A, horizontally striped squares indicate males with disease B, and cross-hatched circles indicate females with both disease A and disease B. In the pedigree, female No. 1 of generation I and male No. 2 of generation I are both diagonally striped symbols, that is, they have disease A but do not show disease B; their daughter, No. 2 of generation II, is a cross-hatched circle, that is, she has both disease A and disease B, including disease B. Reasoning: Two parents who phenotypically do not have disease B gave birth to a daughter with disease B, indicating that disease B does not conform to dominant inheritance, but should appear as recessive inheritance. If it were X-linked recessive inheritance, the father of an affected female usually must have disease B, but male No. 2 of generation I in the figure does not have disease B, so X-linked recessive inheritance can be excluded. Combining the fact that patients with disease B can be female, and that the stem states it is a monogenic genetic disease, it can be judged that disease B is an autosomal recessive genetic disease.
